newsitem.title: USA: USDA says Ellen Haas resigns as undersecetary.
newsitem.headline: USDA says Ellen Haas resigns as undersecetary.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Wednesday said Ellen Haas has resigned her position as Undersecretary for Food, Nutrition and Consumer Services.
Haas had been under fire from Republicans who accused her of mismanaging USDA's huge feeding programs.
Haas' departure is effective Feb. 14, a spokeswoman for the undersecretary said.

Haas had enemies on Capitol Hill who complained she mishandled the transition to healthier school meals. Leaders of the House Agriculture Committee asked last Fall for her to be replaced. Even some of Haas' defenders said she sometimes was too assertive in running the nutrition programs and misplayed relations with Congress.

It had been widely expected that Haas would leave with the beginning of President Clinton's second term although she wanted to stay in office through the implementation of the new welfare reform law which made significant changes in the food stamp program.

As undersecretary, Haas oversaw the food stamp program, school lunches, the popular Women and Infants Feeding Program and several other public nutrition programs. Her portfolio accounted for more than 60 percent of Agriculture Department spending.
